mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days. This relationship holds consistently across all economic regimes without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS levels below 1.0% consistently fail to predict positive 20-day returns with Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 4.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing equity discount rates and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, with Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates robust labor market strength, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline fails to predict positive returns in >40% of cases with interaction Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, strong GDP growth (GDPC1) and high housing starts (HOUST) signal sustained economic momentum, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, GDPC1 and HOUST growth fail to predict positive returns in >50% of cases with Rank IC < 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strengthening manufacturing activity, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth fails to predict positive returns in >55% of instances with Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate below 3.5% signals an overheating labor market that precedes corporate earnings acceleration, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >60% of instances where UNRATE < 3.5% with Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer and housing demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint rise in RSAFS and HOUST fails to predict positive returns in >45% of cases with interaction Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases equity risk premiums, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, FEDFUNDS increases fail to predict negative returns in >55% of cases with Rank IC > -0.03.
